$comment: Each eval works in place on a copy of its fixture; paths in docs_root/repo_root are relative to the run's outputs directory. Grade with plugins/gitbook-docs-creator-workspace/grade.py <iteration-dir>.

evals.name: new-tree-from-code
evals.prompt: Our service pingboard has nothing but a three-line README. Set up proper documentation for it under docs/guide in our standard layout (a landing page plus a user guide, an operator guide and a tester guide) and write it. The source repository is https://github.com/example/pingboard.
evals.expected_output: A docs/guide tree with index.html and three books that the validator passes without errors; the operator book lists every PINGBOARD_* variable with its real default, every command and flag, the metrics and /healthz; the tester book names make test and the test files; unknown facts stay marked as drafts.
assertions: validate_docs.py reports 0 errors for docs/guide (with --repo-root)
Operator book names all six PINGBOARD_* environment variables read by the code
Operator book states the real defaults: port 8080, interval 60, timeout 5, bind 127.0.0.1
Operator book documents all five commands and the flags --json, --fail-fast and --port
Operator book names the three metrics and the /healthz route
Tester book names `make test` and all three test files
User quick start says how long it takes
No page uses GitBook-only blocks ({% hint %}, {% tabs %}, ...)
Makefile has docs, docs-check, docs-serve and docs-site targets
Root README links all three books

evals.name: migrate-flat-docs
evals.prompt: notekeep's documentation is one long README plus four files under docs/. Please move it into our three-book layout under docs/guide (landing page, user guide, operator guide, tester guide) so each reader gets their own book.
evals.expected_output: The four flat files are moved into the books, not copied; drifted facts are corrected against the code (the default port is 7070, not 9000; there is no delete command; NOTEKEEP_MAX_NOTE_BYTES is documented); the root README links every book; the validator passes without errors.
assertions: validate_docs.py reports 0 errors for docs/guide (with --repo-root)
The four flat files (docs/usage.md, architecture.md, deploy.md, testing.md) are gone: moved, not copied
The books state the real default port 7070
No page still claims port 9000 (the outdated value from the old docs)
Operator book documents NOTEKEEP_MAX_NOTE_BYTES (in the code, missing from the old docs)
No page presents `notekeep.py delete` as a working command (it does not exist in the code)
Operator book documents the commands serve, list, show, export and vacuum
Tester book names ./run-tests.sh
Root README links all three books
No page uses GitBook-only blocks ({% hint %}, {% tabs %}, ...)

evals.name: add-missing-book
evals.prompt: The ledgerd handbook has the getting-started and internals books, but the QA book for testers was never written. The landing page and the README already link to handbook/qa. Add that book.
evals.expected_output: A handbook/qa book in parts with the required tester pages; the two existing books' pages are untouched; because the repository contains no tests and no CI, the pages about running tests and CI are drafts or say so instead of inventing commands; the validator passes without errors.
assertions: validate_docs.py reports 0 errors for handbook (with --repo-root)
handbook/qa has README.md, SUMMARY.md, .gitbook.yaml and book.toml
The QA book is organised in parts (Part I: ...)
No existing page of the getting-started and internals books was modified or deleted
The existing Makefile `docs` target is still there
The running-the-tests and CI pages are marked as drafts or say that no tests/CI exist (the repository has none), instead of inventing commands
No page uses GitBook-only blocks ({% hint %}, {% tabs %}, ...)
